big_idea: EXACT change = MONEY PAID minus PRICE. Use careful subtraction.
learning_intention: We are learning to calculate exact change for whole-dollar transactions.
student_learning_goal: I can calculate exact change for whole-dollar transactions.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Pat + Bea — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Money + Price Cards (1 set per pair)

minds_on.hook: Budget Bea: Friends — yesterday we ESTIMATED. Today we CALCULATE EXACT change! Bea opens: 'LINE UP, BORROW, SUBTRACT — that's EXACT!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Bea the Bear puppet (small bear with calculator). 'Money friends — yesterday Pat showed us ESTIMATE. Today: EXACT calculation!'

Define. 'CALCULATE = find the EXACT answer. SUBTRACT = take AWAY one number from another.'

Demo. 'Item $13. Pay $20. CHANGE?'

Write on board: $20 - $13 = ___.

'Subtract column by column. 0 - 3? Borrow from 2: 10 - 3 = 7. Then 1 - 1 = 0. So $7!'

'Bea says — careful column subtraction!'

Demo 4 more:
- $50 - $35 = $15.
- $20 - $14 = $6.
- $100 - $89 = $11.
- $10 - $7 = $3.

'Bea says — check by ADDING. $35 + $15 = $50. ✓'

Now show ESTIMATE check from yesterday. 'Yesterday I estimated $20 - $13 ≈ $20 - $13 = $7. Same! Estimate matched exact!'

'Bea says — estimate FIRST, calculate SECOND, check with addition!'

Now each pair gets Money + Price Cards + Calculator Card. They calculate 4 transactions exactly.

'Bea says — show the SUBTRACTION!'

steps.instruction: Hand out Money + Price Cards + Calculator. Pairs calculate 4 exact changes.

STRATEGY COMPARE: 'Show me YOUR way' beat — pairs solve $20 - $13 by any strategy (count up from 13, take 7 from 20, regroup). Class compares which is fastest. Cite Carpenter & Moser CGI separate-result-unknown.
steps.teacher_prompt: Bea: 'Same exact change, different paths. Pick the one your brain trusts.'

differentiation.for_movement_learners: Walk to compute station. NO-PAPER VERSION: children show subtraction by physically moving cubes from one column to another to demonstrate borrow.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: writes; subtracts; calculates; checks; consistency.

consolidation.exit_routine: Bea's exact change refrain — 'Bea says: LINE UP, BORROW, SUBTRACT — that's EXACT!' (3x). Each child computes one exact change with regrouping shown.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child borrows WRONG in subtraction — repairing the regroup trap at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On exact change with regrouping, the trap is borrow-without-decrement (Fuson on multidigit subtraction) — child borrows across the dollar/cent boundary without decrementing the dollars. Carpenter & Moser CGI separate-result-unknown frames this.

Yesterday Pat estimated. Today Bea calculates exact. Lesson 3 cents-only; Lesson 4 mixed; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Bea asks — let's redo. 0 - 3 — can we? NO. So borrow from 2.'

Probe. '2 becomes 1. 0 becomes 10. Now 10 - 3 = 7. Then 1 - 1 = 0. So $07 = $7.'

Generalise. 'Bea says — when ones digit is too small, BORROW from tens. Reduce tens by 1.'

If still wrong: use $10 + $10 - $13. Take a $10 = $10. From $10 left, subtract $3 = $7. Total $7.
common_misconceptions: Borrow without reducing tens. (Repair: reduce tens by 1.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child borrows but doesn't decrement: drill 'when you borrow, the next column GOES DOWN'; child rewrites.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child can subtract but loses the decimal: drill 'line up the decimals BEFORE subtracting'.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child gets right answer but cannot articulate: force the sentence frame 'I borrowed ___ cents from ___ dollars; the change is ___.'

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of F1.1 exact change.
